text: In 1964, the afterglow of the Big Bang was blamed on pigeons. Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson picked up a strange noise in their giant antenna. Pigeons were nesting inside, leaving droppings. But the noise wasn't the pigeons. It came from every direction in the sky: the afterglow of the Big Bang.
